source.primary_witnesses: Aramaic DSS Astronomical-Book fragments (4Q208-4Q211; late 3rd c. BCE through late 1st c. BCE — the OLDEST surviving Enoch material of any kind) where preserved; Ge'ez (medieval; the only complete witness, but a heavy abridgment of a much fuller Aramaic original) as fallback. NO continuous Greek witness for chs 72-82 — the Akhmim Panopolitanus codex covers only chs 1-32 + the Epistle fragment; a single short Syncellus extract is cited by some scholars for ch 80 but is not extant for the rest of the Astronomical Book.
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly conventions: Aramaic Imperial-Aramaic transliteration per Milik 1976 + Tigchelaar-García Martínez DJD XXXVI 2000 (ḥ ṣ ʿ ḫ); Ge'ez SBL Ge'ez convention (ḫ ḫ̣ ʾ ʿ ä for ä-vowel).
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Milik 1976 DJD apparatus, Tigchelaar-García Martínez DJD XXXVI (2000), Drawnel 2011 The Aramaic Astronomical Book from Qumran, Neugebauer 1985 The Astronomical Chapters of the Ethiopic Book of Enoch (in Black 1985 appendix), and original codicology.
source.fetchedFrom: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch + Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 DJD XXXVI + Drawnel 2011 Aramaic Astronomical Book + Black 1985 Book of Enoch (with Neugebauer 1985 appendix on the astronomical chapters) + Charles 1912 Ge'ez PD + Knibb 1978 Ge'ez critical edition + Nickelsburg-VanderKam 2012 1 Enoch 2 Hermeneia.
source.citation: Milik, J. T., The Books of Enoch (Oxford 1976); Tigchelaar, E. J. C., and García Martínez, F., DJD XXXVI: Qumran Cave 4 / XXVI (Oxford 2000) — official editio princeps of 4Q208-4Q211 with Aramaic Astronomical Book; Drawnel, H., The Aramaic Astronomical Book from Qumran (Oxford 2011) — full critical edition + reconstruction of the Aramaic Astronomical Book; Black, M., The Book of Enoch or 1 Enoch (SVTP 7, Leiden 1985), with Neugebauer's appendix on the Astronomical Chapters of the Ethiopic Book of Enoch; Charles, R. H., The Book of Enoch (Oxford 1912; Public Domain); Knibb, M. A., The Ethiopic Book of Enoch (Oxford 1978); Nickelsburg, G. W. E., and VanderKam, J. C., 1 Enoch 2: A Commentary on the Book of 1 Enoch, Chapters 37-82 (Hermeneia, Minneapolis 2012); VanderKam, J. C., Calendars in the Dead Sea Scrolls (Routledge 1998).
source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 72 — THE SOLAR CIRCUIT through 6 eastern + 6 western gates, daylight/night-length per month. **THE central calendrical chapter of the Astronomical Book — establishes the 364-day solar year that anchors the entire Qumran calendrical tradition (4Q317, 4Q319-4Q330 Mishmarot, 4Q394 MMT calendar polemic, 11Q5 David's-Compositions count).** The Ge'ez of ch 72 is one of the better-preserved sections of the Astronomical Book in the Ethiopic, but 4Q209 fragments (especially 4Q209 frags 6-7 and the 'days of the gates' tables) preserve denser day-count tabulations that the Ge'ez compresses. Where 4Q209/4Q210 preserve parallel material, Aramaic is primary; the Ge'ez Charles 1912 / Knibb 1978 chapter:verse reference is provided as text_geez.

verses.text_geez: መጽሐፈ፡ ሑረተ፡ ብርሃናት፡ ሰማይ፡ ኵሉ፡ በበ፡ ዚአሁ፡ ዘከመ፡ ኮኑ፡ በበ፡ ሕገጊሆሙ፡ ወበበ፡ ጊዜሆሙ፡ ወበበ፡ ስማቲሆሙ፡ ወበበ፡ ምንቅላቲሆሙ፡ ወበበ፡ አውራኂሆሙ፡ ዘአርአየኒ፡ ዑርኤል፡ መልአኩ፡ ቅዱስ፡ ዘሀሎ፡ ምስሌየ፡ ዘውእቱ፡ መርሖሙ፡ ኵሉ፡ ጽሕፈቶሙ፡ አርአየኒ፡ ዘከመ፡ ኮነ፡ ለኵሉ፡ ዓመታት፡ ዓለም፡ ወእስከ፡ ለዓለም፡ እስከ፡ ይትገበር፡ ፍጥረት፡ ሐዲስ፡ ዘይነብር፡ ለዓለም፡
verses.translit: maṣḥafa ḥurata bərhānāt samāy kwəlu baba ziʾahu zakama konu baba ḥəgagihomu wa-baba gizēhomu wa-baba səmātihomu wa-baba mənqəlātihomu wa-baba ʾawrāḫihomu zaʾarʾayanī ʿUrʾēl malʾaku qəddus zahallo məslēya zawəʾətu marḥomu kwəlu ṣəḥfatomu ʾarʾayanī zakama kona la-kwəlu ʿāmatāt ʿālam wa-ʾəska la-ʿālam ʾəska yətgabbar fəṭrat ḥaddis zayənabbər la-ʿālam
verses.witness_primary: Ge'ez (Charles 1912 72:1; Knibb 1978 vol. 2 pp. 167-168) — Aramaic 4Q209 frag 7 col. ii preserves only fragmentary parallels here (Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 pp. 144-146)
verses.witness_secondary: Aramaic Astronomical Book opening lost in DSS; 4Q209 frag 7 ii has lacunose traces only
verses.notes: **INCIPIT of the Astronomical Book / Sefer ha-Mazzalot / Book of the Luminaries.** The title-frame: 'The book of the courses of the luminaries of heaven, each as they are, according to their classes, their times, their names, their origins, and their months, which Uriel the holy angel who was with me showed me — he who is their leader.' **The 'new creation that will endure forever' eschatological frame** anchors the calendrical revelation as cosmic-final-order, not just historical-astronomy. **CROSS-CORPUS**: Uriel as celestial-instruction angel echoes 1 En 21:5, 33:3-4 (Uriel in the Watchers throne-tour). The 'new creation' (fəṭrat ḥaddis) is a Second Temple eschatological motif: cf. Isa 65:17, 66:22 (new heavens and new earth); cf. Jubilees 1:29, 4:26; cf. 1 En 91:16 (Apocalypse of Weeks); cf. Rev 21:1. **The 364-day-calendar tradition's foundation** is announced here — the entire Qumran calendrical system (Mishmarot, MMT, Jubilees) descends from this revelation. Editor: Astronomical Book is a calendar-polemic text — flag the polemical edge for the 2025-month commentary.

verses.text_geez: ወዝ፡ ሕግ፡ ቀዳማዊ፡ ለብርሃናት፡ ብርሃን፡ ፀሐይ፡ ምንቅላቱ፡ በአናቅጸ፡ ሰማይ፡ ምሥራቃውያን፡ ወዐራቢሁ፡ በአናቅጸ፡ ምዕራባውያን፡ ሰማይ፡
verses.translit: wa-zə ḥəg qadāmāwi la-bərhānāt bərhān ḍaḥay mənqəlātu ba-ʾanāqəḍa samāy məśrāqāwəyān wa-ʿarābihu ba-ʾanāqəḍa məʿrābāwəyān samāy
verses.witness_secondary: Aramaic not preserved at this verse
verses.notes: **FIRST LAW: the sun's rising in the eastern gates of heaven and setting in the western gates.** This establishes the 12-gate cosmology (6 east + 6 west) governing the entire chapter. **CROSS-CORPUS**: Mesopotamian astronomical 'gates of sunrise/sunset' through which Shamash enters and exits (cf. MUL.APIN tablet; Enuma Elish V); cf. Ps 19:5-7 (sun emerging like a bridegroom 'from the end of the heavens'); cf. 1 En 33-34, 36 (eastern/southern/western/northern gates seen by Enoch in Watchers tour). **The 12-gates cosmology is one of the most distinctive features of the Astronomical Book** and underlies both calendar and meteorology (cf. 1 En 76 four winds + 12 gates).

verses.text_geez: ወርእኩ፡ ስድስቱ፡ አናቅጸ፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወስድስቱ፡ አናቅጸ፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ይዐርብ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወወርኅሂ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በውስቴቶሙ፡ ወመራኅያነ፡ ከዋክብት፡ ምስለ፡ መሪሖሙ፡ ስድስቱ፡ በምሥራቅ፡ ወስድስቱ፡ በምዕራብ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ በበ፡ ዚአሁ፡ ተራሕው፡ ድኅረ፡ ካልኡ፡ ወብዙኃንኒ፡ ጠባት፡ በኀበ፡ ካልኦቶሙ፡ በኤምነ፡ ወበፅግመ፡ እማንቱ፡ አናቅጽ፡
verses.translit: wa-rəʾku sədəstu ʾanāqəḍa ʾəmənnehomu yəwaḍḍəʾ ḍaḥay wa-sədəstu ʾanāqəḍa ʾəmənnehomu yəʿarrəb ḍaḥay wa-warḫəni yəwaḍḍəʾ wa-yəʿarrəb ba-wəstētomu wa-marāḫəyāna kawākəbt məsla marihomu sədəstu ba-məśrāq wa-sədəstu ba-məʿrāb kwəlomu baba ziʾahu tarāḥwə dəḫra kāləʾu wa-bəzuḫāni ṭabāt ba-ḫaba kāləʾotomu ba-ʾēmna wa-ba-ḍəgma ʾəmāntu ʾanāqəḍ
verses.witness_secondary: Aramaic 4Q209 frag 7 col. iii preserves trace material parallel to the 12-gate enumeration (Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 pp. 146-149)
verses.notes: **THE TWELVE GATES — 6 east + 6 west — through which sun, moon, leaders of the stars all pass.** Enoch sees the gates as ranked-in-sequence with side-windows. **CROSS-CORPUS**: 12-gate cosmology echoes 12-tribe + 12-month structuring; in Rev 21:12-13 the New Jerusalem has 12 gates (3 per cardinal direction). The 'leaders of the stars' (marāḫəyāna kawākəbt) appears here for the first time — picked up systematically in 1 En 82:9-20 (chiefs of seasons, months, days).

verses.text_geez: ወቀዲሙ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ብርሃኑ፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ዘውእቱ፡ ስሙ፡ በአንቀጽ፡ ራብዕ፡ እምነ፡ ስድስቱ፡ አናቅጽ፡ እማንቱ፡ ቀዳማዊያን፡ ምሥራቃውያን፡
verses.translit: wa-qadimu yəwaḍḍəʾ bərhānu la-ḍaḥay ʿabəy zawəʾətu səmu ba-ʾanqaḍ rābəʿ ʾəmənna sədəstu ʾanāqəḍ ʾəmāntu qadāmāwəyān məśrāqāwəyān
verses.notes: **The fourth gate** (of the six eastern gates) is named as the sun's principal rising-point. This is the equinoctial gate — gates 3 and 4 are the two near the equinoxes; gates 1 and 6 the solstice-extremes. The 'great light of the sun' (bərhānu la-ḍaḥay ʿabəy) phrasing recalls Gen 1:16 ('the greater light to rule the day').

verses.text_geez: ወውስተ፡ ይእቲ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ራብዕት፡ እንተ፡ እምኔሃ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ቀዳማዌ፡ ወርኀ፡ ሀለዉ፡ ዐሠርቱ፡ ወክልኤቱ፡ መሣክው፡ ክሥቱት፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ነበልባል፡ ሶበ፡ ይትረኀዉ፡ በበ፡ ጊዜሆሙ፡
verses.translit: wa-wəsta yəʾəti ʾanqaḍ rābəʿt ʾənta ʾəmənnehā yəwaḍḍəʾ ḍaḥay qadāmāwē warḫa hallawu ʿaśartu wa-kəlʾētu masākəw kəśtut ʾəmənnehomu yəwaḍḍəʾ nabalbāl soba yətrəḫḫawu baba gizēhomu
verses.witness_secondary: Aramaic 4Q209 frag 7 iii line 3-5 may preserve fragmentary parallel to 'twelve windows' (Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000)
verses.notes: **TWELVE WINDOWS in the fourth gate** through which the sun's flame emerges. The window-mechanism is a finer-grained device than the gate-mechanism: 12 windows per gate × multiple gates allow the daily-shifting solar position to be tracked. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Mal 3:10 ('windows of heaven'); cf. Gen 7:11 (windows of heaven opened at the Flood). The sun-as-fire-emerging-through-window image is intensely visual.

verses.text_geez: ወሶበ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ በሰማይ፡ ይወፅእ፡ በይእቲ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ራብዕት፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በከመ፡ ሕገጊሁ፡ በውስተ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ራብዒት፡ እንተ፡ ምዕራብ፡ ሰማይ፡
verses.translit: wa-soba yəwaḍḍəʾ ḍaḥay ba-samāy yəwaḍḍəʾ ba-yəʾəti ʾanqaḍ rābəʿt śallāsā mawāʿəla wa-yəʿarrəb bakama ḥəgagihu ba-wəsta ʾanqaḍ rābəʿit ʾənta məʿrāb samāy
verses.notes: **The sun spends 30 days in the fourth gate** (rising) and sets correspondingly in the fourth western gate. This 30-day count is the basis of the schematic-month (360-day base year + 4 epact days = 364).

verses.text_geez: ወበእማንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ይነውኅ፡ መዓልት፡ እምነ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይትዌሰክ፡ መዓልት፡ እምነ፡ ሌሊት፡ ዘእንበለ፡ ይብጻሕ፡ ብርሃኑ፡ ለፀሐይ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ራብዕተ፡ ይነዊኅ፡ መዓልት፡ ቅሩበ፡ ካዕበ፡ ምስለ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይከውን፡ መዓልት፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ክልኤተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወሌሊት፡ ይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ክፋላተ፡
verses.translit: wa-ba-ʾəmāntu mawāʿəl yənawwəḫ maʿālt ʾəmənna lēlit wa-yətwēsak maʿālt ʾəmənna lēlit za-ʾənbala yəbṣāḥ bərhānu la-ḍaḥay ʾanqaḍa rābəʿta yənawiḫ maʿālt qəruba kāʿba məsla lēlit wa-yəkawwən maʿālt ʿaśarta kəlʾēta kəfālāta wa-lēlit yəkawwən ʿaśarta kəfālāta
verses.witness_secondary: Aramaic 4Q209 frag 6 preserves fragmentary day:night ratios (Drawnel 2011)
verses.notes: **KEY: the 12:10 (day:night) RATIO appears here — twelve 'parts' (kəfālāt) of day to ten of night.** This 22-part day = 22 'hours' in the schematic system. **CROSS-CORPUS**: the 18-part day used in some Babylonian astronomical texts; the 12-part day of Egyptian + Hellenistic chronology; cf. Jn 11:9 ('Are there not twelve hours in the day?'). The Astronomical Book uses a peculiar 18-part day in some passages and 22-part in others — Editor will need to handle the inconsistency, which is a scholarly crux (Neugebauer 1985).

verses.text_geez: ወይወፅእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምይእቲ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ራብዕት፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በራብዒት፡ ወይትገብእ፡ ኀበ፡ ኃምስት፡ አንቀጽ፡ በምሥራቅ፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ወይወፅእ፡ እምኔሃ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በኃምስት፡ አንቀጽ፡
verses.translit: wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmyəʾəti ʾanqaḍ rābəʿt wa-yəʿarrəb ba-rābəʿit wa-yətgabbəʾ ḫaba ḫāməst ʾanqaḍ ba-məśrāq śallāsā mawāʿəla wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ ʾəmənnehā wa-yəʿarrəb ba-ḫāməst ʾanqaḍ
verses.witness_secondary: Aramaic not preserved at this verse
verses.notes: **Sun moves from gate 4 to gate 5** — the spring-to-summer progression. Gate 5 = the second-eastern gate moving toward the summer solstice.

verses.text_geez: ወአመ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምነ፡ ኃምስት፡ አንቀጽ፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ይነውኅ፡ መዓልት፡ ወይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ሠለስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወሌሊት፡ ዘጠዐ፡ ክፋላተ፡
verses.translit: wa-ʾama yəwaḍḍəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmənna ḫāməst ʾanqaḍ śallāsā mawāʿəla yənawwəḫ maʿālt wa-yəkawwən ʿaśarta śallasta kəfālāta wa-lēlit zaṭaʿ kəfālāta
verses.notes: **13:9 ratio.** Day grows to 13 parts, night shrinks to 9 (the sun is climbing toward summer solstice).

verses.text_geez: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ምሥራቀ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ውስተ፡ ሳድስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይወፅእ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በሳድስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ሠላሳ፡ ወአሐደ፡ መዋዕለ፡ በእንተ፡ ምልክቱ፡
verses.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay məśrāqa wa-yəbawwəʾ wəsta sādəs ʾanqaḍ wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ wa-yəʿarrəb ba-sādəs ʾanqaḍ śallāsā wa-ʾaḥada mawāʿəla ba-ʾənta məlkətu
verses.notes: **Sun in sixth gate for 31 days — the EPACT-DAY: gate 6 holds the sun an extra day 'because of its sign' (ba-ʾənta məlkətu).** This is the SOLSTICE-EPACT structure: 3 months of 30 + 1 of 31 = 91 days per quarter; 4 quarters × 91 = 364. **The 364-day schematic year is constructed via the EPACT-DAYS at solstices and equinoxes.** Foundation of the Qumran calendar (cf. 4Q317, 4Q319, MMT calendrical-priority polemic).

verses.text_geez: ወይነውኅ፡ መዓልት፡ እምነ፡ ይእቲ፡ ሳድስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ካዕበ፡ ምስለ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይከውን፡ መዓልት፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ወክልኤተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወሌሊት፡ የሐጽጽ፡ ወይከውን፡ ስድስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡
verses.translit: wa-yənawwəḫ maʿālt ʾəmənna yəʾəti sādəs ʾanqaḍ kāʿba məsla lēlit wa-yəkawwən maʿālt ʿaśarta wa-kəlʾēta kəfālāta wa-lēlit yaḥaḍḍəḍ wa-yəkawwən sədəsta kəfālāta
verses.notes: **SUMMER SOLSTICE: day = 12 parts (out of 18); night = 6.** Note the apparent inconsistency: vv. 7-9 use a 22-part day (12+10, 13+9); v. 11 uses an 18-part day (12+6). Neugebauer 1985 explains this as the Astronomical Book using TWO PARALLEL DAY-RATIO SYSTEMS: an 18-part 'Babylonian' system (cf. EAE/MUL.APIN) for solstices/equinoxes, and a 22-part system for monthly ratios. **Scholarly crux** — Editor will flag.

verses.text_geez: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ውስተ፡ ኃምስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይወፅእ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በኃምስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡
verses.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay wa-yəbawwəʾ wəsta ḫāməs ʾanqaḍ wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ wa-yəʿarrəb ba-ḫāməs ʾanqaḍ śallāsā mawāʿəla
verses.witness_primary: Ge'ez (Charles 1912 72:12; Knibb 1978 vol. 2 p. 168) — Aramaic 4Q209 frag 7 col. iii lines 1-3 preserve fragmentary parallel material for the post-solstice descent (Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 pp. 145-147)
verses.witness_secondary: 4Q209 frag 7 col. iii (Aramaic): partial — sun's return through gate 5 (Drawnel 2011)
verses.notes: Sun returns through gate 5 (descending from solstice). 30 days.

verses.text_geez: ወይነውኅ፡ መዓልት፡ ወይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ሠለስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወሌሊት፡ ዘጠዐ፡ ክፋላተ፡
verses.translit: wa-yənawwəḫ maʿālt wa-yəkawwən ʿaśarta śallasta kəfālāta wa-lēlit zaṭaʿ kəfālāta
verses.notes: Day = 13, night = 9 parts. Mirror of v. 9, descending from solstice.

verses.text_geez: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምነ፡ ኃምስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ራብዐ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በራብዕ፡ አንቀጽ፡
verses.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmənna ḫāməs ʾanqaḍ wa-yəbawwəʾ rābəʿa ʾanqaḍa śallāsā mawāʿəla yəwaḍḍəʾ wa-yəʿarrəb ba-rābəʿ ʾanqaḍ
verses.notes: Sun returns to gate 4 (the autumnal-equinox gate). 30 days.

verses.text_geez: ወይትዐረዩ፡ መዓልት፡ ምስለ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይትከበቡ፡ ወይከውን፡ መዓልት፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ወአሐደ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወሌሊት፡ ይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ወአሐደ፡ ክፋላተ፡
verses.translit: wa-yətʿarrayu maʿālt məsla lēlit wa-yətkababu wa-yəkawwən maʿālt ʿaśarta wa-ʾaḥada kəfālāta wa-lēlit yəkawwən ʿaśarta wa-ʾaḥada kəfālāta
verses.notes: **AUTUMNAL EQUINOX: day equals night, 11+11 parts (22-part system).** Equinoctial gate-4 transit.

verses.text_geez: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ውስተ፡ ሣልስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይወፅእ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በሣልስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ሠላሳ፡ ወአሐደ፡ መዋዕለ፡
verses.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay wa-yəbawwəʾ wəsta śāləs ʾanqaḍ wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ wa-yəʿarrəb ba-śāləs ʾanqaḍ śallāsā wa-ʾaḥada mawāʿəla
verses.notes: **Gate 3 for 31 days — the AUTUMNAL-EQUINOX EPACT-DAY.** Symmetric with v. 10 (summer solstice's 31-day gate 6).

verses.text_geez: ወይነውኅ፡ ሌሊት፡ እምነ፡ መዓልት፡ እስከ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ሣልስ፡ ወይከውን፡ ሌሊት፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ክልኤተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወመዓልት፡ ይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ክፋላተ፡
verses.translit: wa-yənawwəḫ lēlit ʾəmənna maʿālt ʾəska ʾanqaḍ śāləs wa-yəkawwən lēlit ʿaśarta kəlʾēta kəfālāta wa-maʿālt yəkawwən ʿaśarta kəfālāta
verses.notes: Night = 12, day = 10. Roles swap as autumn deepens.

verses.text_geez: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምነ፡ ሣልስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ካልዕተ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ምሥራቅ፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡
verses.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmənna śāləs ʾanqaḍ wa-yəbawwəʾ kāləʿta ʾanqaḍa məśrāq śallāsā mawāʿəla
verses.notes: Gate 2. 30 days.

verses.text_geez: ወይነውኅ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ሠለስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወመዓልት፡ የሐጽጽ፡ ወይከውን፡ ዘጠዐ፡ ክፋላተ፡
verses.translit: wa-yənawwəḫ lēlit wa-yəkawwən ʿaśarta śallasta kəfālāta wa-maʿālt yaḥaḍḍəḍ wa-yəkawwən zaṭaʿ kəfālāta
verses.notes: Night = 13, day = 9.

verses.text_geez: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምነ፡ ካልዕት፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ቀዳሚተ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ሠላሳ፡ ወአሐደ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በቀዳሚት፡ አንቀጽ፡ እንተ፡ ምዕራብ፡
verses.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmənna kāləʿt ʾanqaḍ wa-yəbawwəʾ qadāmita ʾanqaḍa śallāsā wa-ʾaḥada mawāʿəla wa-yəʿarrəb ba-qadāmit ʾanqaḍ ʾənta məʿrāb
verses.notes: **Gate 1 for 31 days — WINTER-SOLSTICE EPACT-DAY.** Symmetric with v. 10 (summer) and v. 16 (autumn). Three of the four epact-days are accounted for here (vv. 10, 16, 20); the fourth = vernal-equinox gate-3 (v. 25 below).

verses.text_geez: ወይነውኅ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይከውን፡ ካዕበ፡ ምስለ፡ መዓልት፡ ወሌሊት፡ ይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ክልኤተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወመዓልት፡ ስድስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡
verses.translit: wa-yənawwəḫ lēlit wa-yəkawwən kāʿba məsla maʿālt wa-lēlit yəkawwən ʿaśarta kəlʾēta kəfālāta wa-maʿālt sədəsta kəfālāta
verses.notes: **WINTER SOLSTICE: night = 12, day = 6 (18-part system).** Mirror of v. 11 (summer solstice).

verses.text_geez: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምነ፡ ቀዳሚት፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ካልዕተ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡
verses.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmənna qadāmit ʾanqaḍ wa-yəbawwəʾ kāləʿta ʾanqaḍa śallāsā mawāʿəla
verses.notes: Sun returns through gate 2 (ascending toward spring equinox). 30 days.

verses.text_geez: ወይነውኅ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ሠለስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወመዓልት፡ የሐጽጽ፡ ወይከውን፡ ዘጠዐ፡ ክፋላተ፡
verses.translit: wa-yənawwəḫ lēlit wa-yəkawwən ʿaśarta śallasta kəfālāta wa-maʿālt yaḥaḍḍəḍ wa-yəkawwən zaṭaʿ kəfālāta
verses.notes: Night = 13, day = 9. Mirror of v. 19.

verses.text_geez: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምነ፡ ካልዕት፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ሣልስተ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በሣልስት፡ አንቀጽ፡ እንተ፡ ምዕራብ፡
verses.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmənna kāləʿt ʾanqaḍ wa-yəbawwəʾ śāləsta ʾanqaḍa śallāsā mawāʿəla wa-yəʿarrəb ba-śāləst ʾanqaḍ ʾənta məʿrāb
verses.notes: Gate 3. 30 days. Approaching the spring equinox.

verses.text_geez: ወበይእቲ፡ ጊዜ፡ ይትዐረዩ፡ መዓልት፡ ምስለ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይከውን፡ ሌሊት፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ወአሐደ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወመዓልት፡ ይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ወአሐደ፡ ክፋላተ፡
verses.translit: wa-ba-yəʾəti gizē yətʿarrayu maʿālt məsla lēlit wa-yəkawwən lēlit ʿaśarta wa-ʾaḥada kəfālāta wa-maʿālt yəkawwən ʿaśarta wa-ʾaḥada kəfālāta
verses.notes: **VERNAL EQUINOX: 11+11 parts.** Day and night equalize. Symmetric with v. 15. The cycle has closed.

verses.text_geez: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምነ፡ ሣልስት፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ራብዕተ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ሠላሳ፡ ወአሐደ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ወይወፅእ፡ እምኔሃ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በራብዕ፡ አንቀጽ፡ እንተ፡ ምዕራብ፡
verses.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmənna śāləst ʾanqaḍ wa-yəbawwəʾ rābəʿta ʾanqaḍa śallāsā wa-ʾaḥada mawāʿəla wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ ʾəmənnehā wa-yəʿarrəb ba-rābəʿ ʾanqaḍ ʾənta məʿrāb
verses.notes: **Gate 4 for 31 days — VERNAL-EQUINOX EPACT-DAY (the fourth epact-day).** The four epact-days (vv. 10, 16, 20, 26) are the four extra days that bring the 360-day schematic base year to 364. **Cf. 1 En 75:1-2 (the four leaders of the seasons who guard these epact days); 1 En 82:6 (explicit polemical statement that these four days are 'NOT counted' by those who err)** — Editor: this is the SHARP-EDGE of the Qumran 364-day calendar polemic against the lunar-calendar tradition.

verses.text_geez: ወይነውኅ፡ መዓልት፡ ካዕበ፡ ምስለ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይከውን፡ መዓልት፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ክልኤተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወሌሊት፡ የሐጽጽ፡ ወይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ክፋላተ፡
verses.translit: wa-yənawwəḫ maʿālt kāʿba məsla lēlit wa-yəkawwən maʿālt ʿaśarta kəlʾēta kəfālāta wa-lēlit yaḥaḍḍəḍ wa-yəkawwən ʿaśarta kəfālāta
verses.notes: Day = 12, night = 10. Year has wrapped around — back to the same ratio as v. 7. **The full 12-month cycle has closed.**

verses.text_geez: ወዝ፡ ሕግ፡ ወሑረት፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ወግብአቱ፡ ስብዐ፡ እምነ፡ ሙያኖሙ፡ ግብአቱ፡
verses.translit: wa-zə ḥəg wa-ḥurat la-ḍaḥay wa-gəbʾatu səbʿa ʾəmənna muyānomu gəbʾatu
verses.notes: Summary statement: the law and the course of the sun and its return. **'Seven times its return through its turning'** — likely a corrupted Ge'ez reading; Charles 1912 reads 'sevenfold its course returns through its turnings.' Editor will need to flag the textual difficulty.

verses.text_geez: ወይትዌሰክ፡ ይእቲ፡ ሙያው፡ ለመዓልት፡ ካዕበ፡ ወትትኄፀጽ፡ ለሌሊት፡ በስድስቱ፡ መንገላት፡
verses.translit: wa-yətwēsak yəʾəti muyāw la-maʿālt kāʿba wa-tətḫēḍaḍ la-lēlit ba-sədəstu mangalāt
verses.notes: **The summer-half (six gates ascending): days lengthen, nights shorten.** The 'six paths' summarize the gate-progression 1→6 east + corresponding west.

verses.text_geez: ወትበጽሕ፡ ሙያው፡ ሰማይ፡ መዓልት፡ መዓልት፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ወክልኤተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወሌሊት፡ የሐጽጽ፡ ወይከውን፡ ስድስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡
verses.translit: wa-təbaṣṣəḥ muyāw samāy maʿālt maʿālt ʿaśarta wa-kəlʾēta kəfālāta wa-lēlit yaḥaḍḍəḍ wa-yəkawwən sədəsta kəfālāta
verses.notes: Solstitial extreme restated: day = 12, night = 6 (18-part).

verses.text_geez: ወይትኄፀጽ፡ መዓልት፡ እምነ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይትገብእ፡ ሌሊት፡ እስከ፡ መንገል፡ ስድስት፡ ወይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ወክልኤተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወመዓልት፡ የሐጽጽ፡ ወይከውን፡ ስድስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡
verses.translit: wa-yətḫēḍaḍ maʿālt ʾəmənna lēlit wa-yətgabbəʾ lēlit ʾəska mangal sədəst wa-yəkawwən ʿaśarta wa-kəlʾēta kəfālāta wa-maʿālt yaḥaḍḍəḍ wa-yəkawwən sədəsta kəfālāta
verses.notes: **The winter-half: nights lengthen, days shorten — to the same 12:6 extreme at winter solstice.** Symmetric inverse of v. 30.

verses.text_geez: ወእምዘ፡ ይትዌሰክ፡ መዓልት፡ ለመዓልት፡ ወይትዌሰክ፡ ሌሊት፡ ለሌሊት፡ ወይፈጽም፡ ኆለቆሙ፡ በበ፡ ጊዜሁ፡ ሠለስቱ፡ ምእት፡ ስድሳ፡ ወአርባዕቱ፡ መዋዕል፡
verses.translit: wa-ʾəmza yətwēsak maʿālt la-maʿālt wa-yətwēsak lēlit la-lēlit wa-yəfaṣṣəm ḫolaqomu baba gizēhu śallastu məʾət sədsā wa-ʾarbāʿtu mawāʿəl
verses.witness_primary: Ge'ez (Charles 1912 72:32; Knibb 1978 vol. 2 p. 169) — Aramaic 4Q209 frag 6 may preserve fragmentary parallel to 364-day total (Drawnel 2011 pp. 222-227)
verses.notes: **THE 364-DAY YEAR — STATED EXPLICITLY: 'three hundred sixty-four days.'** This is the calendrical KEYSTONE of the entire Astronomical Book and the foundation of the Qumran calendar. **CROSS-CORPUS**: 4Q317 Mishmarot (priestly courses on the 364-day cycle); 4Q319-4Q330 (calendrical texts assuming 364); Jubilees 6:32 ('364 days'); MMT B (calendrical priority dispute); 11Q5 'David's Compositions' (David composed songs to cover the 364 days of the year). **The 364 = 52 × 7 days = 52 weeks exactly** — every date falls on the same day of the week every year. **Polemical edge**: the 354-day lunar calendar (used by mainstream post-Hasmonean Judaism, eventually adopted by Rabbinic Judaism) is rejected here. Editor: this verse anchors the 364-day-calendar identity-marker of the Qumran community + Enochic tradition.

verses.text_geez: ወይእቲ፡ ናኦተ፡ ሙያው፡ ሙያው፡ ስሉሰ፡ ምእት፡ ስድሳ፡ ወአርባዕቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ዘውእቱ፡ ኆለቅ፡ ለዓመት፡ ዘሐቅ፡ ናኦተ፡ ምሉእ፡
verses.translit: wa-yəʾəti nāʾota muyāw muyāw sǝlusa məʾət sədsā wa-ʾarbāʿtu mawāʿəl zawəʾətu ḫolaq la-ʿāmat zaḥaqq nāʾota məluʾ
verses.notes: **Restatement: 364 = the TRUE FULL YEAR.** The phrasing zaḥaqq ('of truth, of righteousness') is calendrically polemical — the 364-day count is the RIGHTEOUS count. Compare 1 En 82:5-6 (the 'four days that are not counted' polemic).

verses.text_geez: ናኦተ፡ ሙያው፡ ለመዓልት፡ ወለሌሊት፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ወንዕሰት፡ ሙያው፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ዘይትዌሰክ፡ ብርሃኑ፡ ወዘይትኄፀጽ፡ ብርሃኑ፡
verses.translit: nāʾota muyāw la-maʿālt wa-la-lēlit la-ḍaḥay wa-nəʿsat muyāw la-ḍaḥay zayətwēsak bərhānu wa-zayətḫēḍaḍ bərhānu
verses.notes: Summary: the sun's path-of-light waxes and wanes through this annual circuit.

verses.text_geez: ወዝ፡ ሕግ፡ ወሑረት፡ ለብርሃኑ፡ ለዐቢይ፡ ብርሃን፡ ዘፀሐይ፡ ዘርእኩ፡ ወዘስሙ፡ በበ፡ ሕገጊሁ፡ ኮነ፡
verses.translit: wa-zə ḥəg wa-ḥurat la-bərhānu la-ʿabəy bərhān za-ḍaḥay zarəʾku wa-zasəmu baba ḥəgagihu kona
verses.notes: Closing law-summary for the sun: this is the great-light's circuit which Enoch saw, named, ordained.

verses.text_geez: ወብርሃኑ፡ ይትዌሰክ፡ ወይትኄፀጽ፡ በበ፡ ጊዜሁ፡ ኵሉ፡ በበ፡ ሕገጊሁ፡ ወሰዓታቲሁ፡ ኵሉ፡ ይትከውን፡
verses.translit: wa-bərhānu yətwēsak wa-yətḫēḍaḍ baba gizēhu kwəlu baba ḥəgagihu wa-saʿātātihu kwəlu yətkawwan
verses.notes: Solar-luminosity governance restated.

verses.text_geez: ወይእቲ፡ ይእቲ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ዐባይ፡ እንተ፡ ሰብዐ፡ ብርሃና፡ ድልዋ፡ ለወርኅ፡ ብርሃና፡ በዐቢይ፡ ኆለቅ፡ ዘብርሃኑ፡ ይትዐረዩ፡ ሰብዐ፡ ምስለ፡ ብርሃና፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ወይትዌቅሕ፡ ብርሃና፡ ለወርኅ፡ ወሰብዐ፡ ምስለ፡ ብርሃና፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ይትፈቀድ፡ ወይከውን፡ ምሉአ፡ ብርሃና፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ወሰብዐ፡ ምስለ፡ ብርሃና፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ይትፈቀድ፡ ብርሃና፡
verses.translit: wa-yəʾəti yəʾəti ḍaḥay ʿabay ʾənta sabʿa bərhānā dəlwā la-warḫ bərhānā ba-ʿabəy ḫolaq zabərhānu yətʿarrayu sabʿa məsla bərhānā la-ḍaḥay wa-yətwaḳḳəḥ bərhānā la-warḫ wa-sabʿa məsla bərhānā la-ḍaḥay yətfaqqad wa-yəkawwən məluʾa bərhānā la-ḍaḥay wa-sabʿa məsla bərhānā la-ḍaḥay yətfaqqad bərhānā
verses.notes: **Closing verse of ch 72: the sun's light is SEVENFOLD that of the moon (zaḥaqq nāʾota: 7:1 luminosity ratio).** Charles 1912 noted the textual difficulty here; multiple repeats in the Ge'ez suggest scribal corruption. **CROSS-CORPUS**: Isa 30:26 ('the light of the moon will be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be sevenfold' — eschatological reversal). The 7-fold-luminosity formula is also the explicit transition to ch 73 (moon's nature).
